findings.title: WebSocket endpoints lack Origin validation and /v1/system/terminal inherits server secrets into the PTY shell
findings.summary: Both WebSocket endpoints — `GET /v1/system/terminal` (`crates/server/src/system/terminal.rs:17-23`) and `GET /v1/system/live` (`crates/server/src/system/metrics/mod.rs:229-231`) — accept `WebSocketUpgrade` without inspecting the HTTP `Origin` header. In addition, `/v1/system/terminal` spawns `bash -l` via `portable_pty::CommandBuilder::new("bash")` without scrubbing sensitive server environment variables (`ATLAS_TOKEN`, `ATLAS_SHARE_TOKEN`, `DATABASE_URL`) and without bounding concurrent PTY sessions or idle session lifetime.

findings.title: drive/browse.rs snippet() allocates two full Vec<char> copies of extracted PDF text per search result
findings.security_relevance: DoS / memory amplification on large Drive search results
findings.summary: `snippet(text: &str, term: &str)` in `crates/server/src/drive/browse.rs:119-142` collects the entire extracted text of each matching Drive document into `chars: Vec<char>` and a second `lowered: Vec<char>` (8 bytes per character), then runs an O(N*M) `windows(needle.len()).position(...)` scan. `search()` (`crates/server/src/drive/browse.rs:175-191`) fetches full `df.text` (up to `CAP = 200_000` characters per file in `jobs/drive_text.rs:16`) for up to 60 matching files per request, causing up to ~96 MB of transient heap allocations and quadratic worst-case CPU work per search query.

findings.title: Bearer token accepted in URL query string on every /v1 route including terminal, power and mutation endpoints
findings.summary: The global `/v1` authentication middleware (`crates/server/src/auth.rs:13-35`) accepts the master bearer token in the `?token=` query parameter for every route under `/v1`, not only read-only media playback routes. This includes high-privilege endpoints such as `GET /v1/system/terminal`, `GET /v1/system/live`, `POST /v1/system/power/{action}`, and all Photos, Drive, and Share mutation endpoints. Query-string credentials routinely leak into reverse-proxy access logs, browser history, `Referer` headers, and crash/diagnostic traces.

findings.title: decode_aws_chunked_bytes discards chunk signatures and has an integer overflow in slice bounds
findings.summary: `decode_aws_chunked_bytes()` in `crates/common/src/s3.rs:508-535` decodes `STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD` (`aws-chunked`) request bodies by splitting each chunk header on `;` and discarding `;chunk-signature=...` without verifying the chained HMAC-SHA256 chunk signatures. Additionally, line 525 computes `if pos + chunk_size + 2 > input.len()` using unchecked addition, which overflows `usize` on crafted large hex chunk sizes (panicking in debug builds and bypassing the length check to panic at slice indexing on line 528 in release builds).

findings.title: Unbounded Vec batch inputs across Photos and Drive endpoints allow excessive DB and memory load
findings.summary: Multiple batch JSON endpoints accept unbounded `Vec` arrays and pass them directly to PostgreSQL `ANY($1)` clauses or recursive CTEs without checking array length: - `POST /v1/assets/exists` (`crates/server/src/photos/assets/upload.rs:17-32`: `hashes: Vec<String>`) - `POST /v1/assets/{favorite,archive,lock,trash,restore,delete}` (`crates/server/src/photos/assets/state.rs:11-82`: `ids: Vec<String>`) - `POST /v1/drive/move` (`crates/server/src/drive/organize.rs:139-193`: `files: Vec<i64>`, `folders: Vec<i64>`, passed into `WITH RECURSIVE below`) - `POST /v1/drive/trash`, `/v1/drive/trash/restore`, `/v1/drive/trash/delete` (`crates/server/src/drive/trash.rs:16-67`: `ids: Vec<i64>`)

findings.title: Unbounded concurrent pdftoppm execution on Drive thumbnails and unbounded subprocess pipe buffering
findings.summary: `GET /v1/drive/files/{id}/thumb` (`crates/server/src/drive/blobs.rs:106-167`) invokes `pdftoppm` inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` with a 60-second timeout whenever a PDF thumbnail is not yet cached on disk, with no concurrency limit or per-hash deduplication. In addition, `atlas_core::process::output()` (`crates/core/src/process.rs:19-39`) drains both `stdout` and `stderr` with unbounded `pipe.read_to_end(&mut bytes)` in background threads, so a malformed PDF or media file that produces large output can exhaust server memory before the deadline expires.

findings.title: disk-guard.sh sources a mutable state file with fallback to world-writable /var/tmp
findings.summary: `scripts/disk-guard/disk-guard.sh:27-28,82` falls back to `STATE_DIR="/var/tmp/atlas-health"` whenever `HOME` is unset (for example in a systemd unit or CI step) and then executes `[[ -r "$STATE" ]] && source "$STATE"`. Because `/var/tmp` is world-writable and `source` executes arbitrary Bash syntax, a local unprivileged user or compromised container/service could pre-create `/var/tmp/atlas-health/disk-guard.state` and achieve command execution in the context of `disk-guard.sh`.

findings.title: Postgres backup dumps lack restrictive umask and atlas-server systemd/install lack permission and hardening guards
findings.summary: Three operational hardening gaps affect host secret and backup confidentiality: 1. `scripts/pg-backup/backup.sh:23-39` creates `$BACKUP_DIR` and writes `atlas_*.dump` and `globals_*.sql` (containing database roles, password hashes, `api_keys` rows, and user metadata) with the process's default umask (typically `022`, making dumps world-readable). 2. `scripts/atlas/install.sh:9-12` checks that `/etc/atlas/atlas.env` exists, but does not verify or enforce mode `0600` (or `0640` owned by root/atlas) on it. 3. `scripts/atlas/atlas-server.service:7-20` sets no `UMask=0077` or baseline systemd hardening (`PrivateTmp=yes`, `ProtectKernelTunables=yes`, `ProtectKernelModules=yes`, `ProtectControlGroups=yes`), despite holding `/etc/atlas/atlas.env` secrets and running in the `docker` group.

findings.title: Swift API.swift force-unwraps URLComponents and Session.normalize does not restrict schemes to http/https
findings.security_relevance: client crash or unexpected scheme acceptance via atlas://connect deep links
findings.summary: In `app/Atlas/Core/Session.swift:111-119`, `Session.normalize(_ address: String)` prepends `http://` only when `!text.contains("://")`, and does not verify that `components.scheme` is `"http"` or `"https"`. Any scheme containing `://` with a non-empty host (for example `ftp://...` or `file://host/...`) passes `normalize()` and `Session.connectLink(_:)`. Separately, `app/Atlas/Core/API.swift:55-66` force-unwraps `URLComponents(url: ..., resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false)!` and `components.url!`.

findings.title: Sequential DB queries and host subprocess calls in drive/browse.rs and system/host.rs
findings.summary: Several read handlers execute independent database queries or host commands sequentially when they can run concurrently: - `drive/browse.rs:25-89` (`list`): runs the breadcrumb recursive CTE, child-folder totals recursive CTE, and files query one after another on one connection. - `drive/browse.rs:154-201` (`search`): runs name-match files, text-match files, and folder-match queries sequentially. - `system/host.rs:34-108` (`services`): runs `systemctl show` sequentially in a `for` loop per unit, then runs 4 DB queries sequentially, then awaits `app.ml.health().await`.

findings.title: Unchecked Mutex and RwLock unwrap() calls in server request and worker paths
findings.security_relevance: availability (poisoned lock cascades panics across HTTP handlers)
findings.summary: Multiple request handlers and background loops in `crates/server/src/` call `.lock().unwrap()` or `.read().unwrap()`/`.write().unwrap()` on `std::sync::Mutex` / `std::sync::RwLock`. If any thread panics while holding one of these locks, the lock becomes poisoned and every subsequent HTTP request or worker tick touching it will panic in a cascade.

findings.title: Share Worker putManifest buffers full body before size check and parseRange omits safe-integer check
findings.summary: Two defense-in-depth input-handling gaps exist in the Cloudflare Share Worker (`share/src/`): 1. `putManifest()` (`share/src/admin.ts:211-213`) reads the entire request body via `await request.text()` before checking `text.length > MAX_MANIFEST` (8 MiB), rather than rejecting oversized `Content-Length` headers upfront as `bodyLength()` does for file uploads. 2. `parseRange()` (`share/src/range.ts:21-34`) parses arbitrary-length digit sequences with `Number(startText)` / `Number(endText)` without verifying `Number.isSafeInteger(...)`, which loses precision for values above `2^53 - 1`.

findings.title: CLI ssh invocations omit -- host option separator and exec.rs interpolates remote paths unquoted
findings.summary: The CLI (`crates/cli/src/`) passes `ssh_host()` (from `ATLAS_SSH_HOST` or `~/.config/atlas/env`) directly to `Command::new("ssh")` without validating against a leading `-` or passing `--`, and `crates/cli/src/exec.rs:153-168` interpolates `{wd}`, `{tag}`, and `$envf` into a remote shell string without single-quoting. Additionally, `crates/cli/src/config.rs:138-163` reads `~/.config/atlas/env` without warning if it is group/world-readable.
